Comment by al...@bedatadriven.com:

Score: Positive

General Comment:
Great first draft. I think what you're doing is a really good approach for
some of the trickier parts of R --
(1) Translate C to Java
(2) Establish correctness 100% test coverage
(3) Refactor at will!

Line-by-line comments:

File: /trunk/core/src/main/java/r/base/random/RNG.java (r308)
===============================================================================

Line 31: static DoubleVector seeds;
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I have tried to move all the global variables into the Globals class of the
Context object. This will ensure that developers can safely run multiple R
Contexts within a single JVM. (Important for webservers, for example!)

Your primitive implementations can access this by including a @Current
Context context parameter.
Line 38: static double KT = 9.31322574615479e-10; /*= 2^-30 */
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
constants should be marked "static final"
Line 109: RNG_Table[RNG_kind.ordinal()].i_seed[0] ^=
(((RNG_Table[RNG_kind.ordinal()].i_seed[0]) >> 15) & 0377777);
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
One way of approaching this might be to increase the granularity of your
tests--
try writing very small tests in both C and Java to find out where the
divergence arises.

I don't think the bitwise operators treat the sign bit specially so there
should be no difference between C and Java, but you're right there could be
other places where this throws you off.

For more information:
http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/detail?r=308
